title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ས (Derge Tengyur, vol. 107)
shelf_note: Derge Tengyur Madhyamaka section (volume sa / 107), containing canonical Tibetan translation of classical Indian Madhyamaka treatise.

ocr_errors.problem: OCR uncertainty braces and variant notation inserted into word
Spurious hash markers (#) inserted into text and punctuation

tr_errors_A.english: That alone is the ultimate truth. Whatever seeing there is, is a non-seeing.
tr_errors_A.problem: Splits a single relative clause ('seeing ultimate truth itself is non-seeing') into two disjoint sentences

tr_errors_A.english: The wisdom that perceives worldly phenomena does not see everything exactly as it is.
tr_errors_A.problem: Construes wisdom as the agent perceiving worldly phenomena rather than the instrument ('by discernment, all phenomena of transmigrating beings are not seen as they are')

tr_errors_A.english: Therefore, for those practitioners, this is described as being non-deluded.
tr_errors_A.problem: Misconstrues the instrumental agent 'by the non-deluded' (ma 'khrul pa yis) as a passive descriptor of practitioners

pages.prefer_reason: Translation B accurately renders technical Madhyamaka and Pramāṇa terminology and faithfully preserves Tibetan syntactic structures including relative clauses and instrumental agent constructions.

book_verdict: Authentic Derge Tengyur Madhyamaka blockprint page with accurate OCR and faithful translations, with Translation B offering superior philosophical and grammatical precision.
